subject: Business Models
title: Platforms vs Pipelines
description: A quick, practical guide to Platforms vs Pipelines.

hook.text: Traditional businesses are pipelines: make a thing, sell a thing. Platforms don't make anything at all.

buildup.text: A pipeline company like Toyota builds cars. A platform like Uber connects drivers to riders.

discovery.text: Platforms create value by enabling exchanges. They own the marketplace, not the inventory.

twist.text: The world's largest taxi firm owns no cars. The largest hotel chain owns no rooms. Platforms won.

climax.text: Platforms scale faster because adding users costs nearly zero, while pipelines must build more factories.

punchline.text: Own nothing, connect everyone. That's the platform model.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between platforms and pipelines?
options: Platforms enable exchanges rather than making products

details.summary: Traditional pipeline businesses create value in a linear sequence from producer to consumer, while platform businesses create value by facilitating exchanges between external producers and consumers. Platforms scale by orchestrating interactions rather than owning inventory.
details.whyItMatters: Seven of the ten most valuable companies globally are platforms. Understanding why platforms outcompete pipelines explains the defining business shift of the digital era.
takeaways: Pipelines create value linearly; platforms create value through exchanges
Platforms scale by enabling interactions rather than owning assets
Platform businesses often achieve faster growth with lower marginal costs

faq.question: What is the key structural difference between platforms and pipelines?
faq.answer: Pipelines control a sequential process: design, make, sell. Platforms build infrastructure that connects producers and consumers, enabling them to create and exchange value directly. Pipelines own supply; platforms orchestrate supply they don't own.

faq.question: Can traditional pipeline businesses become platforms?
faq.answer: Yes, though the transition is difficult. Nike added a platform layer with its running community. John Deere platforms agricultural data. The key is shifting from selling products to facilitating interactions and data exchange between ecosystem participants.
